INCREMENT 1 — the invariant, proven on the Empire catalogue. The whole deliverable is ONE new vitest file, `src/evaluator/evaluator.corpusLinkLocalChildren.test.js`, written by the test-author (its design is in `testPlan`). Production behaviour does not change in this increment. The implementer's own work is three things: the red/green demonstration of criterion 4, one documentation sentence, and the issue file.

WHAT THE CHECK IS. It derives, from the Empire (definitive) catalogue XML alone, every `entryLink` that declares its own `selectionEntries` / `selectionEntryGroups` / `entryLinks` (exactly 31 of that file's 720 `entryLink`s — measured, see below), builds one roster that holds each of them, evaluates once through the facade (`prepareDataset` + `evaluate`), and asserts that every locally declared child has a report slot directly under the link's own slot. Existence only; nothing about `isHidden`, costs or violations (criterion 3).

MEASURED FACTS (I ran two throwaway Node scripts over the fixture XML — no engine, no vitest; see `testPlan` for the disclosure).
- The Empire (definitive) `.cat` holds 720 `entryLink`s, 31 of which declare their own children. That matches the issue's table exactly.
- 30 of the 31 are `type="selectionEntry"` links; 29 of those are a `Empire Warhorse` link carrying one local `Barding` link, and two are a `Battle Standard Bearer` link (one carrying two local group links `Magic Banners` + `Magic Banners (CoU)`, one carrying a plain local `selectionEntry`).
- The 31st (`29cc-7184-aa01-dc85` `Knightly Orders (WD#310(UK))`, under `Templar Grand Master` `8ab4-17be-8a49-b3f7`) is `type="selectionEntryGroup"` — a bracket, not a selection point.
- Both cases the issue's Log names are present: Captain `6686-1f55-dee3-1bcf` → Warhorse link `f817-432b-7c1a-a8ca` → local Barding link `0535-f68e-b9bc-749b`; and Captain → Battle Standard Bearer link `c9fc-265e-8fa8-b814` → local group links `d938-67af-fe67-684c` / `ca78-a3ea-6bbc-9dc2`, whose member closure is 12 banner links.
- Every one of the 31 chains roots in a top-level `<selectionEntries>` entry of the catalogue, so all 31 are reachable and none needs an 'unreachable' record in this increment (criterion 2 belongs to a later one anyway).
- No locally declared option is shadowed by de-duplication: in no occurrence does another option of the same frame already carry that child's id, `targetId` or resolved target id. So asserting the child's own id is safe for all 31.
- The shared `Empire Warhorse` (`a1e3-7f97-5fc6-abaa`) and `Battle Standard Bearer` (`e9ad-f1ce-aebf-6d23`) targets carry no children at all — every slot the check asserts comes from the link, which is why the class was invisible before PR #214.

DECISIONS.
1. The derivation lives inside the test file, reading the two fixture files with the DOMParser the suite already installs from jsdom. Rejected: `loadCorpus` / `CORPUS_DIRS` from `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.js`. It reads no engine source (so criterion 1 does not forbid it), but it parses all 15 corpus files where two are needed, and a test under `src/` importing `scripts/lib/` crosses a layer the dependency-graph rules police.
2. The expected slots are the ENTRY CLOSURE of the locally declared children, not the child elements verbatim: a `selectionEntry` stands for itself, an `entryLink type="selectionEntry"` for itself, a `selectionEntryGroup` and an `entryLink type="selectionEntryGroup"` for their members (recursively). Grounds, from the format doc alone: a group bundles alternatives (§7.1) and a limit on a group counts its members, not the group (§7.6) — a group is not a selectable thing, so it is not what a slot stands for. Asserting a slot for the group element itself would additionally presume a report-shape rule the check must not encode.
3. The frame an occurrence is measured against is the link itself when it targets a `selectionEntry`, and the nearest enclosing selection (a `selectionEntry`, or an `entryLink type="selectionEntry"`) when it targets a `selectionEntryGroup` — for the same reason as decision 2: a group link has no slot of its own, so its locally declared children stand at the enclosing selection.
4. One `prepareDataset` and ONE `evaluate` over a single roster carrying all 31 occurrences as sibling branches, rather than 31 evaluations (criterion 5, and the memoisation rule of `src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md`). Cross-branch interference cannot cost a slot: slots are never withheld for visibility or an exhausted maximum, and the only mechanism that withholds one is per-frame de-duplication, which each branch faces alone.
5. Slots are located by PATH, not by anchor kind. `AnchorKind` is not exported from the facade, and the facade's own JSDoc documents the `capabilities` key scheme (`/`-joined child indices, occupied slots in roster input order, synthetic anchors appended behind the existing children). So the check computes each frame's path arithmetically from the roster it built and asserts a key exactly one segment deeper.
6. Dataset = the game system `.gst` plus the Empire `.cat` only. The Empire catalogue declares a `catalogueLink` to Mercenaries (`fc47-8392-a6c8-452a`), so the report will carry a missing-catalogue-dependency diagnostic; it is not asserted on, and it cannot affect options under an occupied selection. Loading Mercenaries too would double the parse for nothing.
7. Existence is the whole assertion (criterion 3): no `isHidden`, no violation, no cost, no ordering.

DOCUMENTATION GAP FOUND (implementer task). Criterion 1 names `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` as a source of the expectation, but that document does not state anywhere that an `entryLink` may carry its own children — §7.2 lists only `constraints`, `modifiers` and `costs` as things a link brings along. The normative source is `src/parser/schema/Catalogue.xsd`: `EntryLink` extends `SelectionEntryBase` (lines 396-406), and `SelectionEntryBase` carries `selectionEntries` / `selectionEntryGroups` / `entryLinks` (lines 274-287). Worse, the `§4.4` this repository cites for it (in `ownerDefinitionOf`'s JSDoc in `src/evaluator/evalTree.js`, and in `evalTree.linkLocalChildren.test.js`) does not exist: §4 of that document has no subsections. So the implementer:
- adds ONE sentence to `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §7.2, in the `entryLink` subsection, stating that per `Catalogue.xsd` an `entryLink` extends `SelectionEntryBase` and may therefore declare its own `selectionEntries` / `selectionEntryGroups` / `entryLinks`, which stand at that usage site alongside the target's, and that the real catalogues use it (31 of the 720 `entryLink`s of the Empire catalogue);
- corrects the one dangling `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §4.4 citation in the `ownerDefinitionOf` JSDoc of `src/evaluator/evalTree.js` to §7.2. That comment edit is the only touch to engine source. Leave every other `§4.4` in that file alone — the one at `attachGroupAnchor` points at the design document, not at this one — and leave `evalTree.linkLocalChildren.test.js` untouched.

THE RED/GREEN DEMONSTRATION (criterion 4, implementer). PR #214 changed exactly one production hunk, in `src/evaluator/evalTree.js`: `ownerDefinitionOf` returned `node.def.resolved` for a resolved `entryLink` node and now returns the union of the target's children and the link's own. Isolate that revert and nothing else:

Confirm with `git diff --stat` that only `src/evaluator/evalTree.js` changed and with `git diff` that only `ownerDefinitionOf` did.
2. `npx vitest run src/evaluator/evaluator.corpusLinkLocalChildren.test.js` — record the exit code (expected non-zero) and how many of the 31 cases fail. Expect the one group-typed occurrence (`29cc-7184-aa01-dc85`) to stay green: PR #214 did not touch `offer.js`, whose group-link descent into a link's own children predates it. Do not treat that one green case as a defect of the check.
3. `git checkout -- src/evaluator/evalTree.js`, then run the same command again and record exit 0.
4. Write the command, the revert used, both exit codes and the per-case counts into `docs/issues/0150-corpus-invariant-for-link-local-children/issue.md` (Log, and the decisions above under Decisions; keep the Plan section to this increment's shape). Note there that `evalTree.linkLocalChildren.test.js` also goes red under the revert — expected, and not what criterion 4 asks about.

OUT OF SCOPE, DELIBERATELY. The other 14 corpus files and their 118 occurrences, and any 'unreachable, with reason' bookkeeping (criterion 2). `docs/testing/covered-cells.json`, `docs/testing/worklist.json`, `.claude/skills/evaluator-constraint-explorer/SKILL.md` and `docs/testkatalog-evaluator-e2e.md` (criteria 6 and 7). WHETHER. Tests, and the test IS the deliverable of this increment: one new file, `src/evaluator/evaluator.corpusLinkLocalChildren.test.js`. Framework vitest, level: facade-level integration over real fixture catalogue data. Conventions (German `describe`/`it` titles, English code comments, no mocks, the fixture-memoisation pattern, the `KONTROLLE:` marker) live in `src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md`; load it. It is present and I found nothing in it that contradicts what is asked here.

WHAT THE FILE MAY IMPORT. From the engine: `prepareDataset`, `evaluate` and `DiagnosticKind` from `./evaluator.js`, and nothing else under `src/evaluator/` (criterion 1, ADR 0030, ADR 0033). Plus `readFileSync`/`join` from Node and `JSDOM` from `jsdom` for the `DOMParser`. Its expectation is derived from the catalogue XML, from `src/parser/schema/Catalogue.xsd` (`EntryLink` extends `SelectionEntryBase`, lines 396-406 and 274-287) and from `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §7.1/§7.2/§7.6. Cite those in the file header, not the engine.

THE DERIVATION (in-file, XML only).
1. Read `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/Warhammer Fantasy Battles (6th definitive edition).gst` and `.../The Empire (6th definitive edition).cat` with `readFileSync` (join from `process.cwd()`, as `offer.hiddenGate.test.js` does).
2. Parse both with `new DOMParser().parseFromString(xml, 'text/xml')`. The documents carry a default namespace, so match element names with `getElementsByTagNameNS('*', name)` and, for direct children, filter `element.children` by `localName`.
3. Index every element with an `id` from both documents into one map (game system first, then the catalogue; ids are disjoint GUIDs).
4. OCCURRENCES: every `entryLink` element of the `.cat` that has at least one direct child element inside its `<selectionEntries>`, `<selectionEntryGroups>` or `<entryLinks>` container. There are exactly 31.
5. FRAME of an occurrence: the link itself if `type="selectionEntry"`; otherwise (`type="selectionEntryGroup"`) the nearest ancestor that is a `selectionEntry` or an `entryLink type="selectionEntry"`.
6. ROSTER BRANCH of an occurrence: walk from the frame up to the catalogue root, keeping every ancestor that is a `selectionEntry` or an `entryLink`, and append the frame — root first. `selectionEntryGroup`s are skipped: a roster has no group nodes.
7. EXPECTED SLOT IDS of an occurrence: the entry closure of the link's DIRECT local children. A `selectionEntry` contributes its own id; an `entryLink type="selectionEntry"` contributes the LINK's id (not its target's); a `selectionEntryGroup` contributes the closure of its direct children; an `entryLink type="selectionEntryGroup"` contributes the closure of its resolved target's direct children plus that of its own local children. De-duplicate, and guard cycles with a visited set keyed by element id (key a group link separately from its target).

THE ROSTER AND THE EVALUATION. One roster: `{ forces: [{ defId: 'e821-88b8-2071-6b6a', count: 1, children: [...] }] }` — that is `forceEntry` `Standard (EM-AB)`, declared in the Empire `.cat` itself. One branch per occurrence, in derivation order, each branch the chain of step 6 nested one child per level (`count: 1`, `children: []` at the leaf). No `costLimits`. Then `prepareDataset({ gameSystem, catalogues: [empire] })` and ONE `evaluate(prepared, roster)`, both computed once per file: use the memoisation pattern of the suite doc, or hoist them into `beforeAll(fn, 30_000)` if the default 5 s test timeout would otherwise fall on whichever case runs first. The parse dominates; do not prepare per case.

PATH ARITHMETIC. The facade's JSDoc on `evaluate` is the contract: a `capabilities` key is the `/`-joined sequence of child indices from the root, occupied slots follow the roster's input order, and every synthetic anchor is appended behind the existing children. So the force is `"0"`, branch `i` starts at `"0/i"`, and each further level of the branch appends `"/0"`. FRAME PATH of occurrence `i` = `"0/" + i` followed by `"/0"` repeated `branch.length - 1` times.

CASES.
A. KONTROLLE, the derivation itself: the Empire catalogue holds exactly 31 `entryLink`s that declare their own children. Pins the number criterion 1 names against fixture drift. (For orientation, the same file holds 720 `entryLink`s in total; asserting that number too is optional.)
B. One case per occurrence (`it.each` over the derived list, titled with the link's id and name — keep the title German per the suite doc). For occurrence `i`: assert `report.capabilities.get(framePath)?.defId` equals the frame's id (a self-check that the path arithmetic held), then, for EVERY expected slot id of that occurrence, assert some key of `report.capabilities` that is exactly one segment below `framePath` carries that `defId`. Put the link's name and the missing id into the assertion message — 31 near-identical cases are unreadable otherwise. Assert nothing else.
C. The Barding case, by id: the derivation contains the link `f817-432b-7c1a-a8ca` (`Empire Warhorse`) whose branch is Captain `6686-1f55-dee3-1bcf` → that link, and whose expected ids are exactly `['0535-f68e-b9bc-749b']`; and that slot is present under the link's own path. This is the defect PR #214 fixed.
D. The Magic banners case, by id: the derivation contains the link `c9fc-265e-8fa8-b814` (`Battle Standard Bearer`) under the same Captain, whose direct local children are the two group links `d938-67af-fe67-684c` (`Magic Banners`) and `ca78-a3ea-6bbc-9dc2` (`Magic Banners (CoU)`), whose expected ids number 12, and whose slots are all present under the link's own path. Name at least `14b9-9df2-f13c-f31b` (Imperial Banner), `fa36-4375-131c-3d91` (War Banner) and `7b77-57e3-700b-4bbb` (Banner of Middenheim) literally in the case, so the case still says what it is about if the derivation ever changes.
E. Guard: `report.diagnostics` holds no diagnostic of kind `DiagnosticKind.UNRESOLVED_DEFINITION`. Every `defId` the roster names comes from the loaded documents, so a green run cannot be an artefact of a branch the engine silently dropped. Filter by that kind alone — the report legitimately carries a missing-catalogue-dependency diagnostic, because the Empire catalogue declares a `catalogueLink` to Mercenaries (`fc47-8392-a6c8-452a`) that this dataset does not load. Do not load Mercenaries and do not assert on any other diagnostic.

EDGES, AND WHAT IS LEFT UNTESTED ON PURPOSE.
- `isHidden` is not asserted anywhere (criterion 3): a conditionally hidden child still has a slot, and asserting visibility would re-encode a rule the engine owns.
- Violations, costs, slot ordering and slot count: not asserted. Existence is the whole claim.
- The slot of a locally declared `selectionEntryGroup` itself: not asserted. A group is not a selection point, and whether it gets an anchor of its own is a report-shape rule the check must not presume.
- The other 14 corpus files (118 further occurrences) and any 'no roster can hold this link' bookkeeping: a later increment (criterion 2).
- Empty local declarations: none of the 31 has an empty entry closure, so no case is vacuous. If the derivation ever produces one, let it fail loudly rather than skip.
- One of the 31 (`29cc-7184-aa01-dc85`, the group-typed link under `Templar Grand Master`) is measured against the carrier's slot rather than a slot of its own. That is by design (decision 3 in `plan`), and it is also the one case expected to stay green under the criterion-4 revert.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE. Exactly the two commands in `checks`, from the repository root, after `npm ci`. Nothing else is run for this increment — no linter, no `npm test`, no full E2E: the change is confined to `src/evaluator/` plus two documentation touches, and the root `CLAUDE.md` says the evaluator suite alone judges that.

WHAT IS ALREADY RED. I did not run the suite, not even as a baseline, and no downstream step should read this as one: the first run belongs to whoever runs it. I did run three things, none of them a test: `npm ci` (exit 0), to confirm the environment can run vitest at all, and two throwaway Node scripts in a scratch directory that parse the Empire `.cat` and the `.gst` as text and print the 31 occurrences, their chains, their entry closures and their de-duplication collisions. They import no engine module. They settled three questions the plan depends on — that the derivation reproduces the issue's count of 31, that all 31 chains are reachable from a root entry, and that no locally declared option loses its own id to de-duplication — and every number quoted in `plan` comes from them. They are deleted; nothing of them is in the repository.

SCOPE. This increment adds NO production code. Its whole deliverable is the corpus check itself, which lives in the existing test file src/evaluator/evaluator.corpusLinkLocalChildren.test.js (created by INC-1 for the Empire catalogue alone). The work is to widen that file from one catalogue to all 15 catalogue files of both corpora, to close its books, and to keep it inside the suite's runtime. Everything the file has to contain is specified in `testPlan`; the design decisions behind it are here. Documentation and campaign bookkeeping are INC-3's; nothing outside the test file and src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md changes here.

MEASURED FACTS (all re-derived on this tree with throwaway node scripts, deleted again; nothing in the repo was changed to get them).

1. The corpus still yields exactly 149 occurrences, and the issue's per-file table is exact. Per file: Bretonnia 13, Dark Elves 1, Dwarfs (2005) 5, Forces of Chaos 29, Lizardmen 7, Mercenaries 2, Ogre Kingdoms (definitive) 3, Orcs and goblins (definitive) 9, Skaven 12, The Empire 31, Vampire Counts (definitive) 16 | Dogs of War 5, Ogre Kingdoms (whfb6) 1, Orcs and Goblins (whfb6) 5, Vampire Counts (whfb6) 10. Both .gst files hold 0. Total 149.
2. Every one of the 149 has a frame (the enclosing selectionEntry or entryLink type=selectionEntry): frameOf never fails. Branch depth from the catalogue root: 12 of length 1, 122 of length 2, 15 of length 3. Branch roots sit under the catalogue-level containers selectionEntries (142), entryLinks (5: the root-level 'Campaign/Scenario rules', 'Maneaters', 'Allow experimental rules?' links of Bretonnia, Dwarfs, Ogre Kingdoms, Orcs and goblins) and sharedSelectionEntries (2: the two Mercenaries 'Warhorse' links under Marco Colombo f51e-2e40-a1a6-10aa and Heavy Cavalry 18a2-7e02-a130-068f).
3. Cross-catalogue: every definitive army book carries the same catalogueLink to Mercenaries (targetId fc47-8392-a6c8-452a), and Mercenaries is the corpus's only library catalogue (library="true"). Exactly two shared group targets resolve only there — 6747-35dd-32ed-961a 'Magic Banners (Relics of Lustria)' and 11e7-7d5d-b0fa-1f34 'Magic Weapons (Relics of Lustria)' — pulled in by 18 occurrences across Dwarfs, Forces of Chaos, Ogre Kingdoms, Orcs and goblins, Skaven and The Empire. The whfb6 corpus has no catalogueLink at all.
4. Duplicate ids across a corpus: whfb6 has none; the definitive corpus has exactly two, an infoLink 662a-1b1a-b6df-62ae (Dark Elves / Forces of Chaos) and a constraint dfc9-fce8-cc2a-b997 (Mercenaries / Ogre Kingdoms). Neither is a selection definition, so loading all 11 definitive catalogues into one dataset resolves no definition ambiguously.
5. Runtime and memory of the full prototype, in plain node with jsdom: derivation over all 17 documents 6.3 s; prepareDataset 5.7 s (definitive, 11 catalogues) and 1.2 s (whfb6, 4 catalogues); the 15 evaluate calls 0.85 s in total (largest: Forces of Chaos 227 ms, Vampire Counts 150 ms); 14.5 s wall end to end; peak RSS 1.6 GB on a 16 GB / 4-core box. INC-1 reported ~62 s for npx vitest run src/evaluator, so the expected new figure is roughly 70-80 s.

DECISIONS.

D1 — One prepared dataset per corpus, not one per catalogue. Each dataset is that directory's .gst plus every .cat in it. This resolves the Mercenaries catalogueLink outright, so the criterion's third unaddressable reason ('target resolves only through a catalogue the dataset does not load') never has to be invoked: dependencies are loaded rather than recorded. It also costs two prepareDataset calls instead of 15 and spares 10 redundant parses of the 673 KB definitive .gst. WHETHER. Tests, and only tests: this increment has no production code, so the check itself is the deliverable. It goes into the existing file src/evaluator/evaluator.corpusLinkLocalChildren.test.js, which is rewritten from a one-catalogue check into a corpus-wide one. Framework: vitest, run under the repo's jsdom environment. Titles German, comments English, per src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md.

WHAT THE FILE MUST DO, in the order it does it.

(1) DERIVATION, at module top level, from the raw XML only — the engine is never consulted here. For each of the two corpora (src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive, src/__fixtures__/whfb6): read every .cat/.gst, parse each with `new DOMParser().parseFromString(xml, 'text/xml')`, build one id index over that corpus's .gst plus all its .cat files (first document wins), then, per .cat, take every entryLink that declares its own selectionEntries / selectionEntryGroups / entryLinks (INC-1's directLocalChildren over the three containers of SelectionEntryBase) and produce a PLAIN-DATA record: { corpus, file, id, name, frameId, branch: string[] of definition ids root-first, expected: [{ id, targetId, name }] }. Reuse INC-1's frameOf, rosterBranchOf and entryClosureOf semantics unchanged, with two changes: rosterBranchOf returns ids instead of elements, and entryClosureOf yields { id, targetId, name } per selectable entry (targetId null for a plain selectionEntry, the link's targetId for an entryLink type=selectionEntry). Keep the XML texts (needed by prepareDataset) and drop every document, element and index reference when the derivation ends — no DOM object may survive into a case (D5).

(2) CLASSIFICATION, in the same pass. An occurrence is UNADDRESSABLE, and is recorded as { corpus, file, id, name, reason } instead of being checked, when (a) it has no frame — reason: no roster can legally hold this link; or (b) its catalogue's corpus offers no force at all — reason: the carrier is not reachable from a force; or (c) a locally declared group link's targetId resolves in no document of the loaded corpus — reason: the target needs a catalogue this dataset does not load, naming the target id. All three are empty on today's corpus; they are detectors, not decoration.

(3) THE ROSTERS, one per .cat file, built from the derived records only. Force id by the rule of D2 (own top-level forceEntry; else the corpus .gst's forceEntry plus `catalogueId` = that .cat's root id; else the first force any .cat of that corpus declares — Mercenaries is the only file that reaches the third branch and gets Bretonnia's 3a8b-8c11-beff-0534). The force's children are the occurrence branches in derivation order, each a single chain of count-1 nodes (branchToRosterChild, unchanged). Occurrence i of a file therefore sits at framePathOf(i, branch.length) = '0/i' + '/0' repeated (branch.length - 1) times, unchanged from INC-1.

(4) THE ENGINE, once, in ONE beforeAll with an explicit 120_000 timeout: per corpus one `prepareDataset({ gameSystem, catalogues: [...all .cat texts...] })`, then per .cat one `evaluate(prepared, { forces: [force] })`. Before leaving the loop, reduce each occurrence to the only two things the cases need — the defId the report carries at its frame path, and the list of { defId, targetDefId } of the slots exactly one level below it — and keep the DiagnosticKind.UNRESOLVED_DEFINITION diagnostics per file. Let the prepared handles and the reports go out of scope. No case may call prepareDataset or evaluate.

CASES. Per acceptance criterion of this increment.

A. Coverage of all 15 files, total re-derived (criterion 1 of the increment).
  A1 KONTROLLE: the derived per-file count map deep-equals the frozen table { 'Bretonnia (6th definitive edition).cat': 13, 'Dark Elves (6th definitive edition).cat': 1, 'Dwarfs (2005) (6th definitive edition).cat': 5, 'Forces of Chaos (6th definitive edition).cat': 29, 'Lizardmen (6th definitive edition).cat': 7, 'Mercenaries (6th definitive edition).cat': 2, 'Ogre Kingdoms (6th definitive edition).cat': 3, 'Orcs and goblins (6th definitive edition).cat': 9, 'Skaven (6th definitive edition).cat': 12, 'The Empire (6th definitive edition).cat': 31, 'Vampire Counts (6th definitive edition).cat': 16, 'Dogs of War.cat': 5, 'Ogre Kingdoms.cat': 1, 'Orcs and Goblins.cat': 5, 'Vampire Counts.cat': 10 }. A deep-equal is what makes a drift name its file; the failure message states that the number is re-derived from the corpus and that the issue's table said 149.
  A2 KONTROLLE: the derived total is 149, and the count of .cat files that contributed is 15.
  A3 KONTROLLE: both .gst files hold 0 entryLinks with own local children — the issue's claim that no game-system file has one.

B. The invariant, one case per occurrence (criteria 1, 3 and 5 of the issue). One it.each over all 149 records, titled with corpus, file, link id and link name so a failure names its catalogue. Per case: first the frame self-check — the report's capability at framePathOf(index, branch.length) carries frameId, else the case fails with the computed path in the message, because the child assertions below are worthless without it; then, per expected child, a slot exists exactly one level under that path whose defId is the child's id OR whose targetDefId is the child's targetId (D3). Nothing else is asserted: not isHidden, not effectiveMin/Max, not the slot's order, not its anchorKind. Edges covered by construction: the 12 occurrences whose branch is one node deep (root-level entryLinks such as Bretonnia 8d77-c04d-8bb8-abd9), the 15 three-deep ones, the two Mercenaries occurrences whose branch root is a sharedSelectionEntry (f51e-2e40-a1a6-10aa Marco Colombo, 18a2-7e02-a130-068f Heavy Cavalry), the 18 occurrences whose closure only resolves through the Mercenaries library, and the single-child case (Barding) against the 16-child one (Battle Standard Bearer).

C. The two named cases from INC-1, kept, both against the definitive Empire file. C1 Captain -> Empire Warhorse (f817-432b-7c1a-a8ca) -> Barding: branch ['6686-1f55-dee3-1bcf','f817-432b-7c1a-a8ca'], expected exactly ['0535-f68e-b9bc-749b'], and the slot exists. C2 Captain -> Battle Standard Bearer (c9fc-265e-8fa8-b814) -> Magic banners: branch ['6686-1f55-dee3-1bcf','c9fc-265e-8fa8-b814'], expected 16 children — NOT 12, INC-1's number, because Mercenaries is now loaded — containing at least 14b9-9df2-f13c-f31b (Imperial Banner), fa36-4375-131c-3d91 (War Banner), 7b77-57e3-700b-4bbb (Banner of Middenheim) and the four Relics-of-Lustria banners 02c7-11f9-735b-833a, 1521-23cc-50b1-92ef, c21f-f4f9-f1cf-22cd, 5746-a208-618b-71f6, and every one of the 16 has its slot.

D. The books (criteria 2 and 3 of the increment).
  D1 The books close: recorded.length + checked.length === derivedTotal, all three numbers computed in the run — checked being the occurrences the it.each actually asserted, i.e. the classified-checkable list. Assert the identity itself, and assert derivedTotal === 149 in the same case so the closing sum is pinned to a number the corpus yields.
  D2 Every recorded entry carries a non-empty reason and a file and an id — so a skip can never be silent.
  D3 KONTROLLE: the recorded list is empty today, asserted as a deep-equal against [] so that any future entry is printed in full with its reason. Comment that this is the state D1's dependency loading buys, not a claim that an unaddressable occurrence would be a failure.

E. Guards.
  E1 KONTROLLE: no file's report carries an UNRESOLVED_DEFINITION diagnostic — one case over all 15 files, asserting a per-file map of counts deep-equals all zeros, so a branch silently dropped from the tree (which would shift its siblings' paths) is caught. Other diagnostic kinds are expected and are not asserted: the corpus produces danglingModifierTarget and unresolvedBudgetLimit entries that have nothing to do with this invariant.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT TESTED. The pre-PR-#214 red demonstration (criterion 4 of the issue) — INC-1 did it and it is not repeated. Visibility, hidden state, constraint values, costs, slot ordering and anchorKind — criterion 3 confines the claim to existence. Duplicate-definition diagnostics — the two duplicate ids in the definitive corpus are an infoLink and a constraint, neither a selection definition. The scenario manifests, the coverage records and the campaign documentation — INC-3.

SUITE DOC. src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md exists and its conventions were followed above (facade-only access, no mocks, frozen fixtures, German titles, KONTROLLE prefix for pins, English comments). Two statements in its 'corpus-invariant check' paragraph no longer match what this file does and the test-author corrects them as part of this step: it calls the module-top derivation cheap, which held for two documents but not for 17 (6.3 s measured), and it prescribes indexing elements and deriving from that index, which must now be qualified — the index is built and dropped inside the derivation, and only plain data survives it, because retaining elements pins every jsdom document for the life of the file (1.6 GB peak measured). Add that a corpus-wide check loads one dataset per corpus rather than one per catalogue, so cross-catalogue targets resolve.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE. Exactly one command, from the repository root: `npx vitest run src/evaluator`. Nothing else is run — not the full npm test, not lint, not typecheck, not the single-file run. Report its exit code, its case count and its wall time; criterion 5 asks for the wall time in the record. Expect roughly 70-80 s (INC-1 measured ~62 s at 1560 cases before this file grew) and ~1675 cases.

WHAT IS ALREADY RED. Nothing was run against the suite, by me or for a baseline — a run buys no fact I could not state from reading, and the suite costs a minute. One thing must be expected to fail before it is fixed: INC-1's case D asserts `toHaveLength(12)` for the Battle Standard Bearer closure, and loading Mercenaries makes it 16 (see C2). I did run throwaway node scripts outside the suite — never a test, never a repo file changed, all deleted — to settle three questions the plan turns on and that reading cannot answer: whether the corpus still yields 149 (it does, per file exactly as the issue's table says), whether a slot lookup by defId alone holds across all 149 (it does not — 3 fail, and identity matching by targetDefId fails 0, which is decision D3), and whether the corpus-wide dataset stays inside a plausible runtime (14.5 s wall, 1.6 GB peak, which is decisions D1 and D5).
